name: AnimeThemes
description:
Plugin for Jellyfin that fetches anime themes (OPs and EDs) from animethemes.moe.
**Since the AniDB ID is used to find the matching themes, you'll need to install the AniDB plugin.**
overview: Plugin for Jellyfin that fetches anime themes (OPs and EDs) from animethemes.moe

versions.changelog:
- fix: every version of an OP/ED is downloaded now — shows with several cuts of one theme (v1, v2, …) no longer lose the later ones; the best encode of each version is kept
- fix: theme versions are numbered and listed in order (v1, v2, … v10)
- fix: "Single theme" fetch type prefers the original version when the quality is otherwise equal

- fix: a failing series, an unreadable folder or a library hiccup no longer aborts the theme search for every other item
- fix: existing themes are never deleted over a failed download or unusable API payloads (cleanup runs again on the next successful run)
- fix: a leftover temp file from a crashed run no longer fails its theme forever (ffmpeg overwrites non-interactively now)
- fix: download errors name the file that failed

- fix: the first run for a newly added series no longer aborts the theme search when `theme-music`/`backdrops` don't exist yet
- fix: a single failing series or movie is logged and skipped instead of stopping the run for all remaining items

- fix: theme file names end in `-other`, so Sonarr/Radarr treat them as extras and stop matching theme videos as episodes/movies; Jellyfin theme detection is unchanged and existing files are renamed in place (no re-download)

- fix: theme file numbers are now unique per type (0-01, 0-02 … openings, then insert songs, then endings) — multi-season pools used to show duplicate numbers and a meaningless 0-00 for themes without a sequence
- fix: renaming to the new numbering uses the file's identity (name, marker, size), so renumbering never re-downloads or steals another theme's file
- docs: the Jellyfin web client shuffles background themes on purpose (sortBy=Random); ordering applies to theme lists and clients that keep list order

- fix: only seasons of the same show are collected — spin-offs, movies and remakes no longer leak into a series' theme pool. Series groups on AnimeThemes are franchise-wide, so candidates are filtered by format/title/year and then verified against AniList relations (seasons are prequel/sequel-linked; spin-offs and remakes are not)

- fix: the ordered-name migration can no longer mistake another theme's file for a pre-ordering version of its own (only names that do not themselves look ordered are renamed)
- fix: lookups batch 25 AniDB ids per request instead of 10, keeping large libraries under the API rate limit without retry storms

- feat: multi-season shows are fully covered — the other seasons of a series (its AnimeThemes series and seasons with their own AniDB ids) are queried and their themes collected too
- feat: openings play before insert songs and endings; the theme order is part of the file name (upstream #16)
- fix: existing theme files are renamed to the new ordered names instead of being re-downloaded

- feat: optional loudness normalization (ffmpeg loudnorm) so themes sit at a consistent level next to dialogue regardless of source loudness (addresses upstream #4 and #20)
- feat: numeric volume read-out and finer control (step 0.01)
- feat: the task now reports how many items were skipped for lacking an AniDB provider id (addresses upstream #22 and #19)
- fix: media downloads are paced with a global throttle so parallel runs do not trip the CDN rate limit (addresses upstream #46)
- docs: where theme files are stored and a troubleshooting section

- fix: theme downloads are retried on transient errors — the AnimeThemes CDN sheds parallel load with 503s, which previously failed every download in a burst (the API client had retries, the media client did not)
- fix: download timeouts no longer abort the entire run
- fix: theme downloads now identify themselves with the product user-agent and allow up to 10 minutes for large files

- feat!: theme sync is now always on: every run downloads new themes, removes outdated ones and refreshes replaced content (the "Enforce conformity" option is gone)
- fix: cleanup runs after downloads, so a failed download can no longer remove existing themes
- fix: only files created by the plugin are ever deleted; hand-made theme files are left alone
- fix: partial ffmpeg output is no longer kept as a valid theme (results are finalized atomically)
- fix: theme deletions now trigger a metadata refresh
- fix: invalid include/exclude library regexes abort the run with a clear error instead of crashing
- fix: always keep the newest theme files — the upstream file size is now part of the file name, so content replaced on AnimeThemes is re-downloaded automatically and superseded files are removed

- fix: "Enforce conformity" now re-checks anime that already have themes (picks up newly added themes, removes obsolete ones)
- chore: removed the release-draft workflow so no draft release lingers on the releases page
- fix: type-aware theme download log messages

- feat: support Jellyfin 12 (.NET 10)
- feat: migrate to the AnimeThemes GraphQL API (the JSON:API is deprecated and will be removed)
- fix: correctness, robustness and security hardening
